title: First Light: Handshake & Handoff Notes (soft-release)
content:
Context:
- Small, customer-visible model flip scheduled for early morning window. Goal: minimize blast radius while validating latency/cost regressions and user-facing P0 flows. This is a soft-release: opt-in cohort, gradual traffic increase, explicit handoff to SRE and CS on stable signal.

High-level plan (first-light handshake):
1) Prep (D-2 to D-0)
   - Finalize model bundle and hash, store as pinned artifact: model:v2025-01-11-rl-hf (artifact id in PR).
   - Smoke-run on staging with sample tenant traffic (synth load) for 4h at 90th pct token length; capture tail latency and mem/oom counters.
   - Confirm autoscaler policy tweak: target_util 65 -> 70 for this model (temporary).
   - Notify CS + key customers: send brief note with opt-in instructions and rollback expectations.

2) Window & cohorts (Day-of, 04:00–07:00 PT)
   - 04:00–04:15: Shadow traffic (no routing) for baseline telemetry.
   - 04:15–04:35: Canary cohort A (0.5% synthetic + 1 small real client)
   - 04:35–05:10: Canary cohort B (3%) if A stable
   - 05:10–06:00: Slowfade to 10% (spread across 3 client buckets)
   - 06:00–07:00: Hold at 10% and review; unless clear failures, proceed to scheduled staggered expansion later in day.

Cohort selection rationale:
- Start with clients that have good telemetry and quick rollback paths (dev/test tenants).
- Keep high-volume clients out for now; include one power-user client to validate edge-cases.

Telemetry & pass/fail signals (primary):
- P95 latency (gen-only, compute): threshold 650ms -> fail if > 750ms for >5 consecutive minutes.
- Error rate: generation errors + 5xxs spike >0.6% above baseline for 5m -> fail.
- Token cost drift: >12% increase in tokens consumed for the same prompts (check before/after prompt set) -> investigate.
- Quality smoke: run 150 prompt eval set (seeded) every 15m; automated BLEU/ROUGE-style diff + manual spot-checks. Drop below expected quality metric by >6% -> rollback candidate.
- Resource signals: OOMs on any node, GPU util hotspots >95% sustained for 3 minutes, or autoscaling lag >120s -> immediate rollback.

Operational checklist (on-call & release lead):
- Before flip: confirm monitoring dashboards up, alerting endpoints reachable, runbook link in #releases pinned.
- At each cohort step: annotate the release run in the release tracker (JIRA) with exact timestamps and cohort ids.
- Telemetry owner (Jason) to run live dashboard checks and call out any noise.
- CS owner (Maya) to monitor customer channel and escalate immediate P0s.

Pinning & artifact notes:
- Pin format in config: "model_pin: model:v2025-01-11-rl-hf". Deploy config commit: gh/rt/rollout-config@b3c7d.
- Rolling back: update pin to previous stable tag model:v2024-12-20-stable and push override; the system supports immediate pin override without redeploy.
- Note: we must not change quantization profile mid-rollout. If we need faster footprints, plan a separate rollout for quant changes.

Quick commands (ops cheats):
- Verify current pin: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/configs/release | jq .model_pin
- Force override (emergency rollback): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"model_pin":"model:v2024-12-20-stable"}' https://internal-api.releases.redwood/api/v1/overrides
- Canary-split example (dev CLI): rw release split --from default --to model:v2025-01-11-rl-hf --percent 0.5 --cohort-id CLNT-TEST-1

Communication plan:
- T-30m: Post planned window, cohorts, and quick rollback steps to #releases and #sre. Pin message.
- During window: Release lead posts 15m cadence updates: "04:25 baseline ok; moving to 0.5% cohort" etc.
- If anything crosses threshold: page SRE on-call, then post to #incidents with heading "[RELEASE] immediate rollback recommended: <signal>".

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who will approve an immediate expansion past 10% if metrics are marginal? (proposed: release lead + on-call SRE)
- Should we enable extra caching TTL during the window to reduce cold-start tail? Pros: lowers token cost and latency; Cons: masks model degradation. Suggest: keep standard TTL and log caching hit-rate separately.
- Verify that the dev client used in cohort A has a functioning webhook for immediate canary disable. If not, swap in CLNT-DEV-6.

Backouts & rollback playbook (short):
1) Pause routing to canary cohorts via release control plane (command above).
2) If partial harm observed, pin clients to previous model via per-tenant override API.
3) If system-level issue: full rollback to model:v2024-12-20-stable and scale up stable pool to absorb traffic.
4) Post-action: capture heap profiles, top-10 slow traces, and open a JIRA with severity and timeline.

Post-release (Day+1):
- Hold a 30m triage with SRE, release lead, and perf team to review traces and list follow-ups.
- Update the model catalog entry with measured 95/99 latency, cost delta, and quality delta.
- If stable: schedule staggered expansion plan for 48h later with 25% -> 50% steps.

Personal notes to self:
- Keep the first cohort small and conservative. Resist optimistic expansion without clean telemetry.
- Remember to flag any silent errors (time-limited 429s) — they're sneaky and often missed by high-level error rate metrics.
- Keep one person dedicated to customer comms during window — quick notes defuse panic.

End of file.
